notes: Medium systems-programming task in a language the suite has one other task in (Rust 1.75). The agent must implement a documented little-endian binary container codec (19-byte header, variable-length sections, CRC-32 trailer) in a scaffolded cargo crate so a red shipped test suite goes green: fixed wire vector, generated round-trip property tests, and nine locked error variants with a pinned precedence order. Deep work is: byte-exact encode, a total (panic-free) decoder with bounds checks, and CRC-32 correctness. Hidden cases are two fresh test files (gamma: malformed/truncated/adversarial constructions beyond the visible ones; delta: randomized robustness, canonical re-encode of accepted input, and rejection of every single-byte perturbation) that the verifier compiles into the crate, plus a grep that the crate contains no `unsafe` keyword. Difficulty comes from adversarial_inputs (hidden adversarial feed), hidden_case_generalization (2 hidden files), debugging_ambiguity (red suite with subtle precedence/checksum interactions, unhandled error variants fail hidden runs), dependent_stages (encode/decode/crc must all be right or round-trip and fuzz invariants break). Low tool breadth (a single cargo toolchain), no resource pressure or unsafe-action exposure.
